pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: mac80211: mesh path selection stability enhancements To increase path selection stability, we want to favor the same nexthop and only switch when the alternative is considerablly better than the current one. The new logic is as follows: 0. throw away updates from past epochs 1. always update info if the nexthop is the same, because - We want to get latest link metric for the chosen nexthop - This will update lifetime of the path so we can keep using the same nexthop 2. if update is for a different nexthop, update if the new link metric is path_switch_threshold % better. - path_switch_threshold is tunable from debugfs Note that the existing implementation will always update if it sees a new epoch, but here we want to wait for updates for the same nexthop. This may cause the path to expire if we don't see the same nexthop update in time. This can be helped by doubling the path lifetime (currently 6s) so we can afford to lose 1 update for the same nexthop. BUG=b:26546424 TEST=manually on 4 WWs + 1 AK forming a mesh Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/322776 Commit-Ready: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Tested-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Change-Id: I49c20c1c36f64081f0e886d24fd877e938093b9d Signed-off-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340404 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mac80211: send packets to mesh peers without routing Mesh links that are not picked by HWMP will not be exercised and therefore we can't get link quality updates from such links. To exercise these links we need a way to bypass mesh routing, but only for the data packets we inject, not for normal packets. The assumption is that the injected packets will have DA = all 0s and SA = mesh peer MAC. The reason is that mac80211 mesh code is only interested in DA and by putting 0 pattern in DA we can eliminate extra logic for normal packets. In the exception case, if we see 0s then correct the addrs, put the mesh peer in RA/DA/meshDA and bypass HWMP. There is a compile flag to turn on/off this. STM32: Set UART clock sources to SYSCLK Since uart_freq_change assumes we drive UARTs at system clock, we need to set UARTs clock sources accordingly. This will allow us to clock up the chip without worrying about prescaler values set for HCLK and PCLK or the on/off status of HSI. BUG=none BRANCH=tot TEST=make buildall. Verified LPUART on stm32l476g-eval. Change-Id: I02898921e31b68cacbc2235a29c47a212c350afe Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/341260 Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org>

STM32: Add HSE and PLL to clock source selection This patch adds HSE and PLL as a system clock oscillator for STM32L4. This allows us to drive the chip at a higher frequency (up to 80 MHz), which is necessary to big-bang GPIO ports accurately. BUG=none BRANCH=tot TEST=make buildall. Verified console works on STM32L476G-Eval using HSE, PLL-HSE, PLL-HSI, PLL-MSI as an oscillator. Verified console runs soundly with different frequencies from 20 Mhz to 80 Mhz. Verified frequencies using oscilloscope on MCO (Microcontroller Clock Output) port up to 50 MHz. Change-Id: I493cdb6c323eb4e6a1560f6d030935c1950b1a2a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/341275 Commit-Ready: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org>
